transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you. Um, well, I came in because I just feel... wound up, almost all the time. Like my body is just constantly bracing for the next bad thing to happen. Even when I'm just sitting at my desk at work—I do computer support, which is usually fine, except when people spill coffee on their laptops, which happens way more often than you'd think. I mean, just last week this guy brought in a Macbook that was literally dripping, and he tried to tell me it was just condensation. Condensation! Can you believe that? But anyway, yeah, even when I'm just trying to relax, like going to my dance class on Thursday nights... I love dance, I've been going for three years now, it's salsa mostly... but even there, I can't shake this tense feeling. It's exhausting.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, even when there isn’t a clear reason for concern?

Yeah, constantly. It's like my brain just latches onto things and won't let go. It used to be just about my living situation—I was so stressed about my condo, which has this terrible HOA, by the way. They measure the grass. Literally, with a little ruler. If it's over two inches, you get a fine. Can you imagine having that kind of time on your hands? 

But anyway, my worry doesn't even stay on the condo anymore. It just jumps around to everything. Like, I'll suddenly be convinced my cousin is upset with me because she used a period at the end of a text message. She never uses punctuation! And she just got this new Goldendoodle puppy, which is adorable, but she posts about it like five times a day on Instagram, and I forgot to like one of the pictures, so now I'm thinking she's mad. 

And then from there, my brain will just pivot and I'll start panicking about work, like whether I'm going to make a mistake on a support call. And then it spirals into how I'll ever save money or, I don't know, move forward with my life. Which is impossible right now anyway, have you seen the price of groceries lately? I went to buy avocados yesterday and they were almost three dollars each. Three dollars! For one avocado! I stood in the produce aisle for ten minutes just staring at the sign. How is anyone supposed to save money when produce costs that much? 

So, um... wait, I'm sorry, what exactly did you ask me? Oh, right, if I worry without a clear reason. Yeah. Yes, I do. All the time.
